headline: Turkey's national viticulture symposium met in Tekirdağ, with native grapes and heat stress high on the agenda.
body: The 11th Turkish Viticulture and Technologies Symposium, hosted by the Tekirdağ Viticulture Research Institute with guests from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Bulgaria, heard papers on Öküzgözü from five Elazığ sites, Papazkarası wine yeasts, Kalecik Karası clones and protecting grapes from sunburn. A researcher from the institute said two Thracian producers are close to releasing wine from the revived Karamenüş grape; the next symposium is in Diyarbakır in 2030.
why: It shows where state-backed grape research is heading: native varieties, local yeasts and adapting vineyards to heat. A speaker also named the lack of wine-tourism policy as the main obstacle to that income stream.
